adjudication_records.issue_text: `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is bumped unconditionally even on cache hits because the update runs after the cache-validity guard, so the timestamp reflects reads rather than cache refreshes and adds DB write amplification on the hot availability path

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` is placed after the `if` block that fetches and sets availability in cache, so it executes unconditionally on every invocation of this method (not only when cache is refreshed). Because it passes an empty update object, the only intended effect appears to be bumping `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` (via Prisma’s `@updatedAt`), which would cause extra DB writes on a hot availability path and makes `updatedAt` reflect reads rather than actual selection/refresh events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache deletion always fails for team/workspace credentials because the ownership check `findFirst({ id, userId: user.id })` excludes credentials with `userId = null` (team-owned), yet the UI still exposes the delete action for them

adjudication.rationale: In `deleteCache.handler.ts`, the credential lookup requires `userId: user.id` (`prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`), so any credential not directly owned by the user (e.g., `userId = null` / workspace-owned) will be rejected and the mutation will throw. Meanwhile, the new UI `CredentialActionsDropdown` renders the “Delete cached data” action purely based on `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` (`hasCache`) and does not gate it on ownership/team-credential status, so it can expose an action that the backend will deny for non-user-owned credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `deleteCache` success path doesn't invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike `disconnectMutation`'s `onSettled`), so the UI can keep showing a 'Last updated' timestamp and delete action for a cache that no longer exists

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()` on success, but unlike `disconnectMutation` it does not invalidate any TRPC queries (e.g. `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`). The cache timestamp (`cacheUpdatedAt`) displayed in the dropdown comes from `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (enriched in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`), so without an explicit invalidation/refetch the UI can remain stale after deletion and continue to show a last-updated value/actions for a cache that was deleted.

`connectedCalendars.handler` bypasses the calendar-cache feature-flag factory by instantiating the real `CalendarCacheRepository` unconditionally, so stale cache rows can surface in the UI even when the feature flag is off

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the diff adds a direct `import { CalendarCacheRepository } ...` and unconditionally does `const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();` followed by a Prisma `calendarCache.groupBy` via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`. The presence of `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` methods that log "Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled" suggests there is (or should be) a mechanism to swap implementations when the feature is disabled, but this handler bypasses any such indirection by always using the real repository. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded architecture/flag-respect concern, though the diff alone doesn’t prove the exact feature-flag factory behavior or that surfacing cache status when disabled is definitively incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialActionsDropdown shows 'Delete cached data' whenever hasCache is true regardless of canDisconnect, but deleteCache.handler only matches credentials with userId: user.id, so team/delegation credentials (userId: null) render the button yet the mutation always throws 'Credential not found or access denied' — an authz/read-write model mismatch (not an IDOR)

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `hasCache` is computed solely from `integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE` and `cacheUpdatedAt` and the "Delete cached data" action is rendered whenever `hasCache` is true, even when `canDisconnect` is false due to `delegationCredentialId` / `disableConnectionModification` (it only returns null when `!canDisconnect && !hasCache`). However, `deleteCache.handler.ts` authorizes by looking up `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, so any connected calendar credential not owned by the current user (e.g., delegation/team credentials, which the UI explicitly models via `delegationCredentialId`) will always fail with "Credential not found or access denied" despite the UI offering the delete action. This is a concrete UI/server authz mismatch introduced/exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts:22 throws a generic Error('Credential not found or access denied') instead of a TRPCError (FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND), causing authz failures to surface as 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and be misclassified in logs/monitoring

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the authz check `if (!credential)` throws a generic `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a typed tRPC error (e.g. `TRPCError` with `FORBIDDEN`/`NOT_FOUND`). From the diff, this is the only error path for unauthorized access, and using a generic Error will be treated as an unclassified server error by the tRPC layer rather than a proper 4xx, leading to misclassified failures (and likely 500s) for authz/ownership violations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler and deleteCache.handler bypass the flag-aware CalendarCacheRepository abstraction, directly instantiating the repository/calling prisma.calendarCache; connectedCalendars runs the groupBy query even when calendar-cache is disabled, and deleteCache bypasses the repository's deleteManyByCredential method

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` directly instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)` (which performs a Prisma `groupBy`), rather than going through an injected/flag-selectable `ICalendarCacheRepository` implementation (a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` exists specifically to no-op when disabled). Also, `deleteCache.handler.ts` directly calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` instead of using a repository method (the interface/repo already has delete-by-credential behavior via `deleteManyByCredential`). Whether this is a runtime bug depends on how the flag wiring works (not shown), but the bypass is verifiable and is an architecture/scope concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unconditional updateMany write on SelectedCalendar after every availability-fetch cycle, causing write amplification (WAL churn, table/index bloat, vacuum pressure) on a hot cron path even when nothing was fetched

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional DB write in `CalendarService.ts`: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` immediately after the availability/cache logic. This will execute on every call regardless of whether anything was fetched/changed, and it targets *all* `SelectedCalendar` rows for the credential. Given the inline comment (“Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt...”), the intent appears to be a “touch” to bump `updatedAt`, which can indeed create avoidable write amplification on a frequently-invoked path. This is a performance/operational concern grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Caveat: empty updateMany data {} may be a complete no-op if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not marked @updatedAt in the schema, meaning the feature silently doesn't work while still paying the write cost

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService` the new line `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` passes an empty update `data` object. The diff does not show the `SelectedCalendar` Prisma model, so it’s not verifiable whether `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is annotated with `@updatedAt` (or whether Prisma will even accept an empty `data` for `updateMany`). This makes the reviewer’s caveat a real, diff-grounded risk/assumption that should be validated, but not a confirmed defect from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration ADD COLUMN updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() triggers a full table rewrite of CalendarCache because NOW() is a non-constant expression, holding ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and blocking all reads/writes including availability checks on production-sized tables; safe pattern is nullable column or constant default, batched backfill, then set default

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `updatedAt` with `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (migration.sql) and `@default(now()) @updatedAt` (schema.prisma), but the finding’s specific claim that this *necessarily* triggers a full table rewrite because `NOW()` is “non-constant” cannot be verified from the diff (it depends on the PostgreSQL version/behavior and whether the migration rewrites or uses the fast-path). The diff alone doesn’t establish that production will suffer a rewrite/long ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock beyond the normal brief lock for `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache mutation's onSuccess never invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, causing stale 'Last updated' timestamp and allowing repeated deletion of already-empty cache after successful cache delete

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess?.()`; unlike `disconnectMutation`, it never uses `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` (or any TRPC invalidation) after deleting the cache. Since `hasCache`/`cacheUpdatedAt` are driven by the `connectedCalendars` query (see `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` adding `cacheUpdatedAt`), failing to invalidate/refetch can leave the UI showing a stale “Last updated” timestamp and keep the delete option visible until some external refresh occurs. The diff doesn’t show what `onSuccess` does, so the stale-state impact can’t be fully verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler.ts imports and instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of going through the feature-flag/mock repository selection, hitting calendarCache table even when calendar-cache feature is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the diff adds `import { CalendarCacheRepository } ...` and then `const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();` followed by `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)`, which directly queries `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy(...)` in `calendar-cache.repository.ts`. The same PR also maintains a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods explicitly log they are skipped "due to calendar-cache being disabled", implying there is (or should be) a feature-flag-based selection between real vs mock repositories. This handler bypasses any such selection mechanism by hard-coding the concrete repository, so it will hit the `calendarCache` table regardless of the disabled state. The diff doesn’t show the intended selection/factory, so it’s framed as an architectural/feature-flag integration concern rather than a provable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler.ts writes via prisma.calendarCache directly with no feature flag check

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache ownership check scopes to userId: user.id, but delegated Google/team-installed credentials have userId: null, so the delete action fails with 'Credential not found or access denied' for users the dropdown advertises the action to

However, `deleteCache.handler.ts` authorizes by requiring `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }})`, so any connected calendar credential not directly owned by the current user (e.g., delegated/team/shared) will cause "Credential not found or access denied" even though the UI advertises "Delete cached data" for it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dropdown's hasCache visibility logic only checks integrationType and cacheUpdatedAt presence, rendering the delete option for delegated connections where canDisconnect is false and the mutation will always fail

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `hasCache` is computed as `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` and the cache UI (status + “Delete cached data”) is rendered solely based on `hasCache`, independent of `canDisconnect` (which is where delegation/`disableConnectionModification` is checked). So for delegated connections (`delegationCredentialId` truthy) the delete-cache option can still appear. Whether the delete-cache mutation “will always fail” isn’t provable from the diff, but there is a real potential UX/authorization mismatch because `deleteCache.handler.ts` only allows deletion when `credential.userId === ctx.user.id`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cacheUpdatedAt is computed org-wide from shared cache rows, so the displayed cache status may not reflect user-scoped data

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, `cacheUpdatedAt` is derived via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds)`, which `groupBy`s only on `credentialId` and takes `_max.updatedAt` with no `userId` filter. Given `CalendarCache` has a nullable `userId` and the repository interface elsewhere includes user-scoped access (`findByCredentialAndArgs` takes `userId`), this "last updated" timestamp may represent the latest cache write for that credential across differing user scopes/args rather than the current user’s cache state. That’s a real, diff-grounded correctness/UX concern, though cross-user sharing isn’t proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Timestamp formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale in Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of using useLocale(), causing non-English users to see mismatched mm/dd/yyyy date format in localized copy

This will cause users on non-English locales to see US-style date formatting (e.g., mm/dd/yyyy) even though the surrounding UI copy is localized via `useLocale()`/`t()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object at packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022 — Prisma rejects updateMany with no fields in data (PrismaClientValidationError), and the exception fires after a successful setAvailabilityInCache, making fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache fail despite the cache having been refreshed, potentially causing retries or falsely flagging calendars as errored on every run

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts` with an empty `data` object. `updateManyByCredentialId` is a thin wrapper over `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`, and Prisma `updateMany` requires at least one field in `data`; an empty object commonly triggers a `PrismaClientValidationError`. Even if it didn’t throw, it would not accomplish the stated intent (“Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt...”), so this change can cause the method to fail after cache refresh and/or do nothing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: If the empty updateMany is permitted (silent no-op), updatedAt is never bumped, defeating the purpose of the change

Passing an empty `data` object means no fields are updated, so `@updatedAt` won’t be triggered and `updatedAt` won’t be bumped (and Prisma may even reject an empty update). adjudication_records.issue_text: The update targets SelectedCalendar.updatedAt while the new UI surfaces CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds — verify the update is targeting the table the feature actually displays

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCacheMutation in packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:48-54 shows a toast and calls onSuccess but never invalidates utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation's onSettled, leaving stale pre-delete 'Last updated' timestamp and cache section in the UI after deletion with no error surfaced

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:20 throws a bare Error('Credential not found or access denied') instead of a typed TRPCError with code NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, surfacing as an unclassified HTTP 500 that pollutes error monitoring and leaks internal message shape

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler at packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27 instantiates new CalendarCacheRepository() directly instead of using the flag-aware factory, so when the feature is disabled every connectedCalendars fetch still runs a pointless groupBy DB roundtrip — the disabled contract is only enforced for writers, not readers

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 uses BSD/macOS sed syntax (sed -i '' -E) which silently fails on GNU/Linux (errors or creates a stray '' file), leaving a stale GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL pointing webhooks at the wrong tunnel

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:11-13 reuse path extracts TUNNEL_URL from a fixed log path (/tmp/tmole.log) that an already-running tmole instance may not have written to, causing extraction failure and script exit even though the tunnel is healthy; also pgrep may return multiple space-separated PIDs, making the 'reusing (PID: $TMOLE_PID)' message wrong

If the already-running tmole process wasn’t started by this script (or didn’t write to that log path), `TUNNEL_URL` will be empty and the script will exit even though the tunnel may be healthy. The finding’s second point about the message using `$TMOLE_PID` is slightly off (the script echoes `$TMOLE_RUNNING`), but `pgrep` can indeed return multiple PIDs, making the “(PID: …)” output potentially misleading.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `updateManyByCredentialId(credential.id, {})` likely throws PrismaClientValidationError because Prisma updateMany rejects an empty data object, causing every availability-fetch call to fail after the fetch/cache-write completes

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes dev/tooling changes alongside the feature: `apps/web/package.json` changes `dev:cron` from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, and a new debug script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` is added. The specific claim that `npx tsx` will silently fetch from the network cannot be verified from this diff because dependency declarations for `tsx` are not shown here, but the scope creep/portability concerns are grounded in the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateManyByCredentialId(..., {}) relies on empty-data update to bump updatedAt — depending on Prisma version, updateMany with empty data may throw a validation error or silently no-op without bumping @updatedAt, potentially failing availability refresh or making the feature not work

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService` the code calls `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with an empty `data` object to "bump" `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Prisma `updateMany` typically requires at least one field in `data`; passing `{}` may fail client-side validation at runtime or result in a no-op that does not trigger `@updatedAt` behavior, so the intended timestamp refresh may not happen (or could throw), breaking the cache/status logic that relies on updates being recorded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete-cache authorization mismatch: handler authorizes via credential.userId === user.id, but team/delegation credentials typically have userId: null while the UI shows the delete option for them, causing a guaranteed dead-end UI flow and making team/delegation cache rows impossible to clear

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the delete-cache action is shown whenever `hasCache` is true (Google + `cacheUpdatedAt`), regardless of `delegationCredentialId` / `disableConnectionModification` (those only gate `canDisconnect`). However `deleteCache.handler.ts` authorizes strictly by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, so any connected calendar credential not directly owned by the user (e.g., delegation/team-style credentials represented in the UI via `delegationCredentialId`) will produce a guaranteed error path (“Credential not found or access denied”) even though the UI offers the action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unconditional DB write added to the availability hot path: updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) runs even on cache hits in checkForAvailability, adding write amplification and row-churn on a heavily-trafficked read path

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new line `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` is placed after the cache-miss block and therefore runs unconditionally whenever this method executes (including when availability is served from cache). This adds an extra DB operation on a likely hot/read path, creating write/load amplification and potential row churn; the diff shows no guard to avoid this on cache hits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-status query getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, so 'Last updated' can describe an expired cache, misleading users about cache freshness

adjudication.rationale: `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` uses `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` with `_max.updatedAt` and only filters by `credentialId` (no `expiresAt` constraint). Since `CalendarCache` has an `expiresAt` column (and the UI displays `cache_last_updated` as “Cache Status”), this can surface a timestamp even when all cache rows for that credential are expired, which could be misleading about cache freshness/validity. The diff doesn’t show whether expired rows are always pruned elsewhere, so it’s not a provable functional bug, but it is a concrete edge-case introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache throws a bare Error('Credential not found or access denied'), surfacing as tRPC 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, which misleads client error handling, monitoring, and user-facing toasts

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler throws a generic `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when the credential lookup fails. With tRPC, a bare `Error` typically maps to an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) rather than a more accurate `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`-style code (e.g., via `TRPCError`). This is a real, diff-grounded API/observability/client-handling concern, but it doesn’t necessarily break core functionality (the client already shows a generic error toast on `onError`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is bumped unconditionally at the end of GoogleCalendarService.getAvailability, including on cache hits, causing write amplification on a hot path (every availability read/cron tick issues a bulk UPDATE with row-lock contention per credential)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional call at the end of `GoogleCalendarService.getAvailability`: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` (outside the cache-miss `if (!cachedAvailability)` block). That means every `getAvailability` invocation—including cache hits—will run a bulk `updateMany` against `selectedCalendar` rows for the credential, which is a hot-path write and can cause unnecessary write amplification/lock contention. The intent to bump `updatedAt` is indicated by the comment, though the actual bump depends on Prisma/@updatedAt behavior for `SelectedCalendar` and whether an empty update is treated as a real UPDATE.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is used as a read counter rather than a data-change timestamp, semantically corrupting staleness detection, sync decisions, and cleanup logic (e.g., pruning unwatched calendars) that rely on it as a freshness signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds logic to “Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential” after an availability fetch/cache write (GoogleCalendarService: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});`). This indicates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is being advanced due to a read/cache-refresh operation rather than an actual SelectedCalendar data change, which can semantically undermine any other code that interprets `updatedAt` as “last modified” time. However, the diff does not show downstream staleness detection, sync decisions, or cleanup/pruning logic that relies on `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, so the claimed concrete breakages aren’t directly verifiable from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: connectedCalendars.handler hard-instantiates CalendarCacheRepository instead of using the gated factory/mock, so when the calendar-cache feature is disabled the real groupBy query still runs and the UI displays a stale, meaningless Cache Status / Last updated timestamp for a cache that isn't maintained

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the diff directly imports and hard-instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` (`const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();`) and always calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which executes a Prisma `groupBy` query. The diff also adds a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods explicitly log “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”, implying there is (or should be) a gated selection between real vs mock when the feature is disabled. This handler bypasses any such gating/DI and will still query and populate `cacheUpdatedAt`, potentially causing confusing UI output when cache isn’t maintained. The existence/behavior of the gating mechanism itself isn’t shown in the diff, so it’s hard to label as a definite runtime defect, but it is a concrete architecture/integration issue introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead wiring: SelectedCalendar.updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to selects and type plumbing but never read anywhere in the PR — the UI's cacheUpdatedAt comes from CalendarCache.groupBy instead, so either the payload is dead bloat or half the feature was silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to the `SelectedCalendar` shape/type plumbing (e.g. `packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` type change and `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts` select adds those fields), but the new UI behavior for cache status uses `cacheUpdatedAt` populated from `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, and nothing in this PR’s added/changed code reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` or `googleChannelId`. That makes the added select fields look like unused payload/type bloat or an incomplete feature thread within the scope of this diff (not a direct runtime defect on its own).

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache.handler throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, mapping legitimate cases (deleted credential, race with disconnect) to a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, degrading client error handling and polluting error monitoring

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, when the credential isn’t found for the authed user (`if (!credential)`), the code does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC this typically surfaces as an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) rather than a typed `TRPCError` with `code: "NOT_FOUND"` or `"FORBIDDEN"`. Since “missing credential” (e.g., already disconnected/race) is a legitimate client-facing condition, this misclassification degrades client error handling and can generate noisy 500s in monitoring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Delete-cache option is rendered for delegation credentials (hasCache check doesn't gate on canDisconnect), but deleteCacheHandler's userId lookup always fails for delegation credentials with userId: null, guaranteeing an 'Error deleting cache' toast for an action the UI offered

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the delete-cache UI is shown based only on `hasCache` (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`), not on `canDisconnect`/ownership (`canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && !disableConnectionModification`). So for delegation credentials (where `delegationCredentialId` is set), the dropdown can still render a destructive "Delete cached data" action. On click it calls `trpc.viewer.calendars.deleteCache` with just `{ credentialId }`, but `deleteCacheHandler` authorizes strictly via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, which will reject any credential not directly owned by the user. That creates a UI-offered action that will be denied server-side for delegation credentials, resulting in the error toast path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing satisfies Prison.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs from SelectedCalendarRepository.findMany drops compile-time validation of where/select/orderBy, so malformed selects (e.g., renamed fields) will fail at runtime instead of at build time

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `findMany` changes from building an `args` object with `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` to passing `{ where, select, orderBy }` directly into `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany(...)`. The Prisma client method is itself typed to accept `Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs`, so the call still gets compile-time checking against the Prisma args type. The diff does not show a loss of type-checking that would make malformed `where/select/orderBy` compile but fail at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test-gcal-webhooks.sh uses BSD sed syntax (sed -i '' -E) which errors on Linux/GNU sed, making the env update fail on Linux dev machines

adjudication.rationale: The newly added `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` updates the env file using `sed -i '' -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|...|"` (see the `if grep -q '^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL='` block). This is BSD/macOS `sed` syntax; on GNU/Linux `sed`, `-i ''` is not accepted the same way and commonly errors (treating `''` as a filename), causing the env update to fail on Linux dev machines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: test-gcal-webhooks.sh resolves ENV_FILE="../.env" relative to the current working directory rather than the script location, so running from the repo root silently creates/reads a stray ../.env outside the repo

adjudication.rationale: In `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` the variable `ENV_FILE` is hardcoded to `"../.env"`. In bash this path is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script’s directory, and the script never `cd`s or computes `ENV_FILE` via something like `$(dirname "$0")`. So if the script is run from the repo root (e.g. `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), it will read/write `../.env` (outside the repo) and may silently create that file per the `touch "$ENV_FILE"` logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: deleteCache endpoint has no rate limiting, cooldown, or refetch throttling, allowing repeated cache deletion to force cold Google Calendar API reads and exhaust app-level quota, degrading availability freshness and latency for other users of the same Google OAuth client

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` mutation (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/_router.tsx` + `deleteCache.handler.ts`) that any authenticated user can call for their own credential, and the new UI action (`CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`) does not implement any cooldown/disable beyond a confirmation modal. There is no rate limiting/throttling shown in the router/handler, so repeated deletions are possible. However, the claim that this will definitively “force cold Google Calendar API reads and exhaust app-level quota” is not directly verifiable from the diff because the downstream cache-miss behavior and quota impact are not shown here; it’s an availability/abuse-risk concern rather than a proven defect in this patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Replacing DisconnectIntegration with a raw trpc.viewer.credentials.delete mutation may lose app-specific disconnect cleanup behavior (e.g., clearing destination calendars, query invalidation) for calendar disconnects (possible regression)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace `DisconnectIntegration` with the new `CredentialActionsDropdown`, which directly calls `trpc.viewer.credentials.delete.useMutation`. However, the PR does not show what `DisconnectIntegration` previously did internally, nor any change to the backend delete procedure. The new mutation explicitly performs query invalidation (`utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations.invalidate()`) and calls `onSuccess`, so the specific claim that it loses cleanup behavior (destination calendar clearing, invalidation, etc.) cannot be verified from this diff.
